title: A bootstrap JWT with the wrong issuer or type falls through to standard Keycloak auth and is rejected without a valid session
description: authenticateOnboarding.js verifies the token with { issuer: 'vibrantix-onboarding' } and requires decoded.type === 'onboarding'; on any verify/type failure it delegates to the standard authenticate middleware rather than granting access.
steps: Craft a JWT signed with the correct JWT_SECRET but issuer='some-other-issuer' and type='onboarding'
Call GET /api/v1/onboarding/state with 'Authorization: Bearer <that JWT>' and no Keycloak session
expectedResult: The bootstrap verification fails (wrong issuer), falls through to Keycloak authenticate, and — with no valid Keycloak token present — the request is rejected with 401.

title: Protected onboarding endpoints reject requests with no Authorization header
steps: Call GET /api/v1/onboarding/state with no Authorization header
Call POST /api/v1/onboarding/steps/step-1/complete with no Authorization header
expectedResult: Both requests are rejected with 401 { error: { code: 'UNAUTHORIZED', message: 'No token provided' } } before any controller logic or DB access runs.

title: orgId for onboarding state is derived solely from the authenticated JWT, ignoring any client-supplied orgId
description: onboarding.controller.js reads req.orgId (populated by the auth middleware from the token claims) for both getState and completeStep — it never reads an orgId from req.body/req.query/req.params. Confirms a forged orgId in the request cannot redirect a write to another org's OnboardingState (IDOR guard).
preconditions: Valid bootstrap/Keycloak token for User A of Org A
Org B exists with its own OnboardingState
steps: As User A (Org A), call POST /api/v1/onboarding/steps/step-1/complete with a JSON body additionally containing { orgId: '<Org B id>' }
Fetch Org B's OnboardingState directly to check for unauthorized modification
expectedResult: The completion is recorded against Org A's OnboardingState (from the token), not Org B's — the extraneous orgId field in the body has no effect.

title: Concurrent signups for the same domain cannot both succeed (unique index race)
description: signup.controller.js relies on a Mongo unique index (E11000 -> DOMAIN_TAKEN/EMAIL_TAKEN) rather than an application-level pre-check-then-insert, which is the correct pattern to avoid a TOCTOU race under concurrent requests.
steps: Fire two POST /api/v1/onboarding/signup requests concurrently with the same domain and different emails
expectedResult: Exactly one request succeeds (201); the other returns 409 DOMAIN_TAKEN — no two Organization documents are created for the same domain.

title: Platform tour update requires both orgId and userId resolved from auth context before any write
description: onboarding.controller.js updatePlatformTourStatus (the live, second definition) returns 401 if either req.userId or req.orgId is missing, before touching PlatformTourState.findOneAndUpdate.
steps: Call POST /api/v1/onboarding/platform-tour/update with a token/session that resolves userId but not orgId (or vice versa)
expectedResult: The request is rejected with 401 UNAUTHORIZED and no PlatformTourState document is created or modified.

title: Public onboarding endpoints expose no cross-org data
description: onboarding.routes.js exposes GET /frameworks, POST /signup, and the DIY /request, /verify-otp, /complete-activation endpoints without auth by design. They must only ever return public catalog data (active compliance frameworks) or act on the specific email/OTP supplied — never leak another organization's OnboardingState, users, or setup progress.
steps: Call GET /api/v1/onboarding/frameworks unauthenticated and inspect the response payload
Attempt to pass an arbitrary orgId/email query parameter to /frameworks and /signup to see if it changes the response scope
expectedResult: GET /frameworks returns only the public compliance-framework catalog (name/title/description/region/version) with no org-specific or user-specific fields; extraneous query parameters have no effect on response scope.
